items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: I have seen presidents from Franklin Delano Roosevelt. And each succeeding one. And Roosevelt I liked a lot.

ctx.x: You seem to be an astute observer, and I wonder what you think of what the state of our country at this moment? © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

I have seen presidents from Franklin Delano Roosevelt. And each succeeding one. And Roosevelt I liked a lot. I liked John F. Kennedy a lot. And I am absolutely crazy about Barack Obama. I thought he was the closest to my heart that ever got elected. But of those three, those are the only three that I favored. I didn’t even favor Kennedy as my favorite candidate at that time. There was somebody else — Adlai Stevenson was in that race and I thought Adlai Stevenson would have been a more appropriate choice. But…

items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: I remember when President Roosevelt brought us into the war. I remember hearing those things on the radio.

ctx.x: So your grandmother didn’t say, “Now Warren, don’t you be going in those blues clubs” or anything.

Well you know we had those cautionary warnings, but I mean it was the fact that we were so exposed to a wide range of people. People coming in town and out of town from other places were rotating through the family, and there were discussions of politics at that early age. I remember discussions about Communism and Socialism, and by 1942 — I remember when President Roosevelt brought us into the war. I remember hearing those things on the radio. We didn’t have any television in those days.
Yeah, because you were about six or seven, something like that?
